headline: U.S. Central Command (CENTCOM) has issued an update on operations against Iran in the region. CENTCOM also reports that "nearly 150" ships have been redirected, with 5 noncompliant vessels disabled, in support of the U.S. naval blockade of Southern Iran, preventing an estimated $30 billion in crude oil exports. The blockade has also been complemented by the recently established Task Force-Iron Gate (TF-IG) to "synchronize efforts to stop illicit movement of advanced weapons systems, dual-use technologies, sanctioned materials and illegal revenue streams" along Iran's land borders and Caspian Sea coastline.

headline: Two properties in Gloucestershire are being searched in a Russia espionage probe involving a U.S. Army member. British counter-terrorism police arrested the 41-year-old near Gloucester on Tuesday, November 10. He remains at a London police station. The arrest falls under Sections 1 and 3 of the National Security Act 2023. Counter Terrorism Policing leads the investigation alongside MI5, the U.S. military and the FBI. FBI Director Kash Patel called the allegations of the utmost concern. Brig. Gen. Sean Stinchon of U.S. Army Counterintelligence Command credited the joint work with UK authorities and warned that insider threats remain persistent. - BBC News
